notes: Background: mid-market product analytics SaaS with EU customers and strict data residency requirements (financial vertical customers).
Primary ask: start on Hosted API (fast integration) -> migrate to Dedicated for predictable latency + EU-only data residency and auditability.
Workload: chat-based product assistant for end users (conversational support), embeddings for semantic search across docs and personalization, and reranking for recommendation pipelines.

Performance targets: aim for p99 chat latency <= 250ms within EU region for 99% of requests; throughput ~40-60 reqs/s for typical weekday traffic; embeddings batch throughput ~200 qps during periodic reindexing.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget, wants clear Dedicated reserved vs burst delta; asked for cost-per-conversation and estimated monthly token volumes.
Data residency: cannot allow raw user content leave EU for storage or inference. Procurement requires a written EU-only residency SLA and audit log access for last 12 months.

Multi-region routing question: interested in active-passive multi-region failover (EU primary, fallback to US for DR) but wants cert that PII won’t be persisted outside EU unless explicitly triggered.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-02): 'We need predictable tail latency for the assistant; occasional cross-region fallbacks make legal nervous.'
POC notes: configured hosted API endpoints in eu-west, enabled KV/prefix caching; saw 15-20% token cost savings with prefix cache for search flow; reported p99 spikes when cold-starting large models.
Security ask: SSO (SAML) integration, SOC2/ISO27001 evidence, KMS integration for key control, retention_controls to meet customer retention windows.
Current plan: complete security Q by 2026-03-15, SE Hugo to deliver Dedicated sizing + per-region latency simulations, follow-up call to finalize pricing (AE Sofia) by 2026-03-25.
Open items: need concrete latency numbers for Dedicated (eu-west only) at requested throughput, explicit language on data flows for multi-region fallback, Dedicated commit tiers for mid-market.
